planning_note: Leaf stateful module computing a 7‑bit CRC with asynchronous reset and enable‑controlled update. Organised around declaration, combinational pre‑computation, and sequential register update.

structural_blocks.purpose: Declare the 7‑bit CRC register and any internal stored or derived objects.
structural_blocks.placeholder: // skeleton only: declaration of CRC register (width 7) and supporting storage/wires
may_appear: combinational wire for inv (if not local to a later block)
retrieval_focus: register width, reset value, update condition

structural_blocks.purpose: Combine BITVAL and CRC[6] to produce inv combinationally.
structural_blocks.code_shape: continuous assignment or combinational always block
structural_blocks.placeholder: // skeleton only: combinational compute of inv = BITVAL ^ CRC[6]
must_appear: expression for inv using BITVAL and CRC[6]
retrieval_focus: XOR input path, dependency on CRC[6]

structural_blocks.purpose: Asynchronously reset or enable‑updated CRC register using inv and current state.
structural_blocks.code_shape: synchronous always block with asynchronous reset
must_appear: enable‑gated update of CRC[0] <= inv, CRC[3] <= CRC[2] ^ inv, CRC[i>0,i!=3] <= CRC[i-1]
hold behaviour when Enable is low
may_appear: local assignment to simplify shift‑XOR mapping

semantic_modes.meaning: RST asserted – CRC forced to 0 irrespective of Enable
Enable deasserted, RST inactive – CRC retains current value
Enable asserted, RST inactive – CRC advances according to shift‑XOR rule

state_model.notes: Output directly driven by register; no additional output stage

global_invariants: CRC is always a valid 7‑bit value
inv is purely combinational and appears only as a next‑state input
RST overrides any Enable activity (reset priority)
open_semantic_questions: None – spec fully defines update equations and corner cases.

responsibilities: Provide the CRC register and any global‑scope storage for use by other blocks.
coupling_rules: B2 reads CRC[6]; B3 reads the full register and drives it
forbidden_drift: do not add extra state registers or delayed versions of CRC

responsibilities: Compute inv as BITVAL XOR CRC[6] combinationally.
timing_semantics: zero‑delay combinational; must be stable before the active clock edge
coupling_rules: feeds inv signal to B3; must recompute on any change of BITVAL or CRC[6]
forbidden_drift: do not register inv; do not create sequential dependencies here

responsibilities: Implement the asynchronous reset, enable‑gated shift‑XOR register update.
timing_semantics: asynchronous reset: CRC <= 0 when RST high
synchronous update on rising CLK: if Enable high, apply shift‑XOR rule; otherwise hold
touched_objects: CRC (driven), RST, Enable, CLK, BITVAL (indirectly via inv)
coupling_rules: consumes inv from B2; reads current value of CRC from B1 for shift
forbidden_drift: do not soften the reset priority (RST overrides Enable)
do not add pipelining or extra clocked stages

chosen_decisions.decision: Separate declaration, combinational pre‑computation (inv), and sequential update into distinct blocks.
chosen_decisions.reason: Keeps retrieval straightforward and allows local reasoning about each concern; matches the explicit spec separation of inv and register update.

deferred_decisions: exact coding style for the sequential block (single always vs. separate reset/update) – not forced by spec, left for generation.
structural_risks: None; the decomposition is minimal and naturally follows the design.
behavioral_risks: None; all corner cases (Enable deassertion, simultaneous RST/Enable) are explicitly defined and must be enforced in generation.
